opportunities.title: The Hardware Wallet Supply Chain Is the New Attack Surface — and 'Buy From Us Directly' Isn't a Fix
opportunities.why_now: Ledger confirmed a physical LTE implant in reseller units that drained an estimated $86M, and Trezor is now cutting resellers in Asia as a 'preventative' measure — the industry is admitting the box itself can't be trusted.
opportunities.angle: Security explainer: walk through how the implant worked, why tamper-evident packaging failed, and give readers a concrete verification checklist (open-box photos, seal checks, direct-from-manufacturer only) — end on 'this was always the weak link, you just didn't want to believe it.'

opportunities.title: Anthropic Just Said the Quiet Part: Self-Spreading AI Malware Is Coming for Wallets Next
opportunities.why_now: Anthropic's warning about autonomous 'AI worms' lands days after a hardware implant drained $86M in seed phrases — the next version of that attack won't need a physical box.
opportunities.angle: Forward-looking threat piece: map the AI-worm warning onto crypto-specific attack vectors (auto-draining smart contracts, self-propagating clipboard hijackers, AI-authored phishing kits) — framed as 'priced in' inevitability, not hypothetical.

opportunities.title: Coinbase Wants to 'Start the Quantum Fix Now' — Translation: Your Bitcoin's Security Model Has an Expiration Date
opportunities.why_now: Coinbase, holder of 5% of all BTC, is publicly pushing for post-quantum migration design work to begin immediately, a rare admission from an incumbent that current cryptography has a shelf life.
opportunities.angle: Skeptical breakdown: separate real cryptographic risk timeline from marketing urgency, explain what 'flexible designs' actually means technically, and tell readers what (if anything) they should do with cold storage today vs. in 5 years.

opportunities.title: A UK Court Just Ruled Chinese Law Decides Who Owns $5B in Seized Bitcoin — Your Jurisdiction Was Never Yours
opportunities.why_now: The UK High Court's ruling that Chinese law governs claims over $5B in seized BTC is a landmark custody/jurisdiction precedent that most holders haven't priced into their risk model.
opportunities.angle: Legal-risk explainer for self-custody and exchange users: what this ruling implies for asset recovery, cross-border seizure exposure, and why 'not your keys, not your coins' doesn't save you from state-level jurisdictional claims.

opportunities.title: Chainalysis Just Won Its Blockchain Forensics Credibility Fight in Court — Again. Here's Why That Matters More Than the Hack Headlines
opportunities.why_now: Chainalysis Reactor surviving a Daubert challenge on appeal cements onchain tracing as admissible, courtroom-grade evidence — quietly more consequential than any single hack story this week.
opportunities.angle: 'Already priced' framing: explain that privacy-via-obscurity on public chains is now legally dead weight, tie it to mixers/privacy coins' declining utility as a shield, and tell readers what actually still works for operational privacy.
